goal: Allow querying transaction history by address or script directly in Bitcoin Core
Lets wallet frontends and node operators retrieve history without third-party indexing software
Operates with minimal disk overhead and functions on pruned nodes
agreement: Concept approval without stated reasons (sedited, l0rinc, w0xlt)
Verified by unit, functional, and manual regtest testing (kravens)
Unaddressed objection: declaring TxToJSON in a common header violates library boundaries (kravens)
Open safety concern: query budget ignores block and undo reads, risking excessive disk I/O (kravens)

categories.name: rpc
why: P2 because it allows querying script history directly without running external indexers
Solves a long-standing feature gap requested across many previous attempts

categories.name: utils
why: P3 because it introduces order-preserving integer serialization infrastructure
Provides secondary serialization plumbing primarily needed to support the new index
